title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Page 127 opens a section titled 'Graphes MD', where MD means Mumford–Deligne. It sets up the combinatorics of the boundary stratification of the stable-curve moduli spaces M̄_{g,ν}. The previous page enumerated stable graphs for small (g,n) by hand, with codimensions and incidence arrows; this page gives them an axiomatic form.

(1)–(2) A weighted graph is a tuple (S, Â→, o, σ, g):
- S is a finite set of vertices.
- Â→ is a finite set of 'arcs', i.e. half-edges.
- o: Â→ → S is the origin map.
- σ is an involution of Â→.
- g: S → ℕ is the genus labelling.

(3) Edges are Â = Â→/σ. The fixed points I = (Â→)^σ are the 'arêtes libres' (free edges), i.e. legs or marked points. The 2-element orbits are the ordinary edges ('liens'), so A = A→/σ ≅ Â \ I. The drawing shows legs as arrows, and the genus label g_i is omitted when it is 0.

(4) Stability condition: 2g_s + ν̂_s ≥ 3 for every vertex s, where ν̂_s = #o^{-1}(s) is the total valence ('ordre total'). Equivalently, g_s = 0 forces ν̂_s ≥ 3 and g_s = 1 forces ν̂_s ≥ 1. A margin note names graphs satisfying (4) 'stables'.

(5) ν̂_s = ν_s + ν_{s→}. Here ν_s counts ordinary half-edges at s ('ordre réduit') and ν_{s→} counts legs at s ('ordre complémentaire', corresponding to the marked points of the curve).

(6) ν(G) = card I is the number of marked points.

(7) c(G) = ½ Σ ν_s is the number of ordinary edges, called the 'modular codimension'. It is the codimension in M̄_{g,ν} of the stratum of curves with dual graph G, i.e. the number of nodes.

(8) g(G) = Σ g_s + h¹(G) is the 'virtual genus'. It is the arithmetic genus dim H¹(X, O_X) of a nodal curve with dual graph G, for G connected.

The next page continues:
- d(G) = 3g−3+ν, the 'dimension modulaire'.
- 'Homomorphisms of generalization' G → G'. These consist of a vertex map S → S' and a half-edge map to Â' ⨿ S'. They must be compatible with σ and o on the retained half-edges B (which contain all legs). The contracted half-edges C are sent to vertices. B must be in bijection with the half-edges of G', and S/R in bijection with S'. Each fibre subgraph G_0(s') must have virtual genus equal to g_{s'}.

These are exactly edge-contraction morphisms of stable graphs, i.e. specialization relations between boundary strata. Overall purpose: a combinatorial model of the stratification of M̄_{g,ν}, as the indexing category for the Teichmüller groupoids / 'tour de Teichmüller' studied in this file.
errors: (8) gives the arithmetic genus only for connected G. For a disconnected graph, Σg_s + h¹(G) differs from 1−χ(O_X) by h⁰(G)−1. Grothendieck flags this himself with the 'connexité de G' annotation and the margin note on π₀(G).

Minor: the stability condition (4) is stated vertex-wise without requiring G connected, although c, d and g as dimension data only make sense for connected G. Otherwise the formulas (stability, c = ½Σν_s, genus, d = 3g−3+ν) are correct.

ideas.what: Graph as (vertices, half-edges, origin map, involution) with the fixed points of the involution as legs/marked points, plus a genus labelling of vertices
ideas.modern_name: Stable graph in the half-edge ('flags/tails') formalism
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kontsevich–Manin (1994, graphs τ=(F,V,∂,j) with tails = fixed points of j); Getzler–Kapranov, Modular operads (1998). The involution-without-fixed-points version is Serre, Trees (1977); dual graphs go back to Deligne–Mumford (1969)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the stratification of M̄_{g,n} and the Teichmüller tower informally, but I know of no formal half-edge definition there

ideas.what: Stability condition 2g_s + ν̂_s ≥ 3 at each vertex
ideas.modern_name: Stability of a weighted dual graph (vertex-wise Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen stability)

ideas.what: Number of edges c(G) = codimension of the stratum; d = 3g−3+ν; virtual genus Σg_s + h¹(G)
ideas.modern_name: Codimension of boundary strata / arithmetic genus of a nodal curve

ideas.what: 'Homomorphismes de généralisation' (next page): contraction morphisms between stable graphs, with connected fibres whose virtual genus equals the target vertex genus
ideas.modern_name: Contraction/specialization morphisms in the category of stable graphs (modular operads, graph categories)

missed.claim: A complete formalization of Deligne–Mumford stable graphs appears here. It uses half-edges with an involution whose fixed points are the legs, plus a genus labelling and the vertex-wise stability condition. The next page adds the contraction morphisms with the genus-of-fibre condition. This is essentially the Kontsevich–Manin / Getzler–Kapranov formalism, written well before 1994–1998 if the dating ('à partir de 1978', Teichmüller-groupoid period ~1981–84) holds.
missed.quote: σ : Â→ → Â→ une involution ... les autres sont dites arêtes libres ... Conditions de stabilité MD : ∀s∈S, on a 2g_s + ν̂_s ≥ 3
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority point for the combinatorial category underlying modular operads and tropical moduli. It shows Grothendieck had the indexing category of the boundary stratification of M̄_{g,n} precisely in hand while designing the Teichmüller tower.

missed.claim: The stable-graph category is explicitly set up as the combinatorial skeleton for the Teichmüller groupoids of the file. The previous page enumerates strata for small (g,n) with codimensions. This ties the 'tour de Teichmüller' directly to what is now the modular-operad / graph-complex structure on M̄_{g,n}.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The Esquisse's tower is usually linked to the modular-operad / Grothendieck–Teichmüller literature only retrospectively. Here the link is explicit in Grothendieck's own hand.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is standard today. But a fully axiomatized half-edge stable-graph formalism with contraction morphisms, in Grothendieck's hand and probably predating Kontsevich–Manin and Getzler–Kapranov by about a decade, is a notable unpublished detail. It is not deep new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: 'σ renvers. de l'arc opposé [?]' likely reads 'σ: renversement (l'arc opposé)', i.e. σ sends an arc to the opposite arc.
(5) should read ν̂_s = ν_s + ν_{s→}, with ν_{s→} = card of I at s (I = Â→^σ). The labels are 'ordre total', 'ordre réduit' and 'ordre complémentaire' (marked points).
'arêtes ordinaires {+ou liens+}': the insertion is 'ou liens'. The struck words before 'arêtes libres' include 'bandes' and 'relatives'.
